text:
kate: Heads up — after last night's driver push to 535.113 in east2 the MIG partitions disappeared from ~10 nodes. Pods that request gpu-mig are failing allocation. :frowning:

anil: ugh. which nodes? any common kernel or kubelet versions?

kate: nodes: gpu-east2-01..10. Kernel 5.15.0-1019 everywhere, kubelet 1.26. Logs show `nvidia-smi -L` returning only host GPUs (no MIG instances). `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` yields 'No MIG devices found'.

lucy: @anil can you check if nvidia-mig-manager / nvidia-hostd are running? last time a hostd restart fixed a few machines.

anil: checking now... grabbing SSH to gpu-east2-03.

infra-bot: deploy-job 2026-03-18 02:15:12 — driver-upgrade-535.113 rolled to east2 pool (batch 1/3).

anil: on gpu-east2-03: hostd service active but `journalctl -u nvidia-hostd` shows repeated: "MIG device list changed, but profile restore failed: uuid mismatch". Kernel modules are loaded: nvidia, nvidia_uvm. `lsmod | grep nvidia` looks normal.

kate: "uuid mismatch" rings a bell — past CUDA bumps changed the persistent GUID mapping. Are nodes showing different device UUIDs compared to the cluster registry?

anil: yes, `nvidia-smi -q | grep UUID` reports host UUIDs that don't match the kubelet's device-plugin recorded IDs. Kubelet device plugin is the upstream nvidia-device-plugin v0.13.2. It had registered MIG devices before the upgrade.

tim: did we also bump nvidia-operator / mig-manager sidecars? If driver upgrade happened without operator update, the operator might try to reconcile with an older mapping.

lucy: operator is still at 1.8.0 (image nv/operator:1.8.0). The driver image changed to nv/driver:535.113. There was a note in the rollout about skipping the operator bump to reduce blast radius.

anil: quick mitigation: cordon + drain affected nodes and fallback to older nodes. But we have limited capacity in east2 for requests that require MIG. Planning rolling-restart of nvidia-hostd + device-plugin on one node to test.

kate: try this sequence on a single node (tested on staging before):
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-hostd
kubectl delete pod -n kube-system -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-east2-03
# wait for kubelet to re-register devices
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi mig -lgip
```

anil: ran it. After hostd restart, hostd logged "restored MIG profiles from cache" then immediately: "cache entries skipped: uuid mismatch (expected MIG-0 but saw GPU-1-host-uuid)". Device plugin pods restarted but still register only host GPUs.

tim: could be the driver changed the naming/UUID scheme for MIG slices. Check presence of `/etc/nvidia/mig/` and any cached mapping files in `/var/lib/nvidia/`. Also `modinfo nvidia` to confirm build matches kernel.

anil: `/var/lib/nvidia/mig/` contains old snapshots referencing MIG IDs like MIG-3-2048g. New driver logs show different index offsets. I suspect the driver change shifted NVML indexing.

lucy: two potential paths: rollback driver to 535.86 (previous) while we validate mapping, or update nvidia-operator + mig-manager to the new release that understands the new indexing. Which is faster?

kate: rollback is fastest short-term but risky if some nodes already have processes bound to new kernels. Operator update requires image promotion + canary. I prefer rolling two nodes with operator update in canary then operator reconciles mapping.

anil: opened a mitigation playbook in the incident runbook: cordon -> drain -> rollback driver image on drained node -> uncordon. Trying rollback on gpu-east2-04 to confirm pods recover.

deploy-bot: rollback-request 1823456820 accepted for node gpu-east2-04 (driver -> 535.86).

anil: after rollback on gpu-east2-04, `nvidia-smi -L` shows MIG instances again and pods are scheduled. So rollback is effective.

kate: good. let's keep rollback as short-term. For long-term we need to validate operator + mig-manager compatibility with 535.113 and update the operator images and unit tests to catch UUID/index shifts. Add an automated smoke-check for `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` after driver rollouts.

lucy: I'll open a PR to bump nvidia-operator + mig-manager images, add CI test that runs a simple MIG restore on upgraded driver image. Also adding a preflight job in the rollout pipeline to run `nvidia-smi -L` and compare to cached mappings.

tim: also let's add a script in infra repo to snapshot `/var/lib/nvidia/mig/` and NVML mapping before any driver rollouts. That should help fast-compare post-upgrade.

kate: thanks team. I'll keep the remaining east2 nodes on rollback plan until operator canary finishes. Postmortem + action items to follow. :memo:

infra-bot: incident 2026-03-18-01 created — MIG partitions unavailable in east2 after driver upgrade. Assigned: anil, lucy.
